overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by discussing the Train Depot in executive session on July 28 under Purpose 6, and its later consent-agenda vote did not cure that violation; the AG ordered compliance and release of minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board entered executive session on July 28 for an improper purpose, based on discussions of the Train Depot under Purpose 6.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review of the executive session minutes, we find that the Board’s discussions were not appropriate under Purpose 6 because the discussions did not relate to the purchase, exchange, lease or value of real property.

allegations.summary: The Board argued that its August 4 consent-agenda vote approving an MBTA application cured any executive session violation.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, this action was insufficient to fully address and remedy the violation committed.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements.
Release to the public the portion of the July 28 executive session minutes that pertain to the Train Depot discussions, without any redaction or withholding.
Certify to the Attorney General within 30 days of the letter that the executive session minutes portion has been released.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to release to the public that portion of the July 28 executive session meeting minutes that pertain to the discussions involving the Train Depot.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
